Noun

  • (Received Pronunciation, General American, Canada) IPA: /ˈvɛd͡ʒ.tə.bəl/, [ˈvɛd͡ʒ.tə.bɫ̩]
  • (UK, dialectal) IPA: /ˈvɛd͡ʒ.ə.tə.bəl/, [ˈvɛd͡ʒ.ə.tə.bɫ̩]
  • (US, Canada, dialectal) IPA: /ˈvɛt͡ʃ.tə.bəl/
  • (Australia, New Zealand) IPA: /ˈved͡ʒ.tə.bəl/, [ˈved͡ʒ.tə.bɫ̩]
  • (North India) IPA: /ˌvɛdʒɪˈʈebəl/
  • (South India) IPA: /ˈvɛdʒɪʈəbɪl/

vegetable (plural vegetables)

  1. (archaic) Any plant.
  2. A plant raised for some edible part of it, such as the leaves, roots, fruit or flowers, but excluding any plant considered to be a fruit, grain, herb, or spice in the culinary sense, and usually including non-plants lumped into the same culinary category, such as edible mushrooms and seaweed.
    Synonyms: (informal) veg, (informal) veggie
  3. The edible part of such a plant.
    Synonyms: (informal) veg, (informal) veggie
  4. (figuratively, often derogatory) A person whose brain (or, infrequently, whose body) has been damaged to the point that they cannot interact with the surrounding environment; a person in a persistent vegetative state.
    Synonym: cabbage
  5. (RAF, slang, historical) A mine (explosive device).

Alternative forms

  • vegitable (obsolete)

Etymology

From Middle English vegetable, from Old French vegetable, from Latin vegetābilis (“able to live and grow”), derived from vegetāre (“to enliven”). Displaced Old English wyrt and ofett, whence modern wort and ovest.

Related to vigil, vigour, vajra, and waker.
